conviction_note: Four dated primary-document findings all point one way, but the stock is already at its 52-week low after a 28% week, so I sized each well below what it would be worth on an unmoved tape; -8.5 is roughly half the 18.2% median historical reaction and just above the 9.09% deadband, which is the honest place for a coherent-but-partly-priced negative cluster on a $0.2m/day name.

findings.finding: The Q2 call on 2026-09-11 is a 'pre-recorded conference call and webcast' — the first pre-recorded RENT earnings call in at least four quarters; the Q2 FY25 (2025-08-25), Q4 FY25 (2026-03-24) and Q1 FY26 (2026-05-19) announcements all said 'conference call and live webcast', so management has removed live analyst Q&A for this print while the company is run by an interim CEO.
findings.why_not_priced: Every calendar aggregator carries this release as a date row ('RENT reports 9/11 BMO') and no vendor field encodes call format, so the word 'pre-recorded' in paragraph two is invisible to screens. If the market had focused on it there would be at least one note or headline framing the format change; instead the only coverage of the 2026-08-21 release is the date itself (StockTitan headline 'Rent the Runway to Report Q2 2026 Results Sept. 11'). The 25-delta skew cannot have absorbed it either — the baseline records no options market on this name at all, so there is no priced directional statement anywhere.
findings.independence: Corroborated by an independent primary document with no overlap: the 2026-09-01 8-K establishing a $10m incremental term loan, i.e. management raised money and then removed the venue where it would be asked why. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1468327/000095010326013373/dp252774_8k.htm

findings.finding: RENT borrowed a $10,000,000 incremental term loan on 2026-09-01 'for working capital and other general corporate purposes' — ten days before the print and after the 2026-07-31 quarter end — even though the 10-Q states the minimum liquidity covenant was PERMANENTLY REMOVED by the First Amendment of 2026-01-28 and the Second Amendment of 2026-04-01 already lets it PIK interest until 2027-05-03; with no covenant to cure and no cash interest to service, the only reason left to take sponsor money is operating cash, which implies a Q2 cash balance far below the $37.1m at 2026-04-30 and the $43.6m at 2025-07-31.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-01 (Third Amendment to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, dated 2026-09-01; NOT the Oct 2025 A&R, the Jan 2026 First Amendment or the Apr 2026 Second Amendment)
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public and the stock has fallen, so the fact of the loan is partly in; what is not in is the arithmetic, which needs three documents read together. RENT burned $26.8m of cash in Q2 last year ($70.4m at 2025-04-30 to $43.6m at 2025-07-31); even at half that rate on the cut inventory plan, cash at 2026-07-31 lands near $20-27m against $157.1m of long-term debt and a $92m market cap. If the market had done that sum the stock would not need the print to find the number, and there would be a note somewhere stating a Q2 cash estimate — there is none, because the baseline notes this name is not well covered and there is no option chain to express it in.
findings.independence: Partly self-limiting and I am flagging it rather than hiding it: the $6m cash component of the 2026-09-03 settlement (finding 3) was agreed two days after this loan, so roughly $3.1m of the $10m is plausibly earmarked for that and is NOT operating burn — which is exactly why I sized this at -3.0 rather than at what a pure working-capital read would justify. Independent corroboration of the burn trajectory itself, from a different filing: Note 3 of the 2026-06-03 10-Q, cash $37.1m and operating cash flow $(3.8)m versus $8.3m a year earlier. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468327/000146832726000031/rent-20260430.htm

findings.finding: On 2026-09-03 RENT signed a $9,000,000 Stipulation and Agreement of Settlement of the November 2022 IPO securities class action — $6m cash plus $3m in Class A stock, with insurers paying ~$2.9m and the company ~$3.1m — eight days before the print and five weeks after the 2026-07-31 balance sheet date, so under recognised-subsequent-event treatment the charge lands in the Q2 GAAP numbers being reported on 2026-09-11, and the stock component is ~1.1m new shares (~3.3%) on a 33.59m share count.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q1 10-Q filed 2026-06-03 carried NO accrual for this case — it recited only the boilerplate that losses are accrued when probable and estimable — so any model built off the last filing has zero dollars in it for a charge that is now signed and quantified. The settlement was agreed after the quarter closed and after the earnings date was announced, so it cannot be in consensus by construction. If it were priced there would be a revised GAAP loss estimate in circulation; on a name with essentially one analyst there is not.
findings.independence: Rests on a different document from findings 1, 2 and 4. The absence of a prior accrual is confirmed from a separate filing, the Q1 FY26 10-Q legal proceedings note. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001468327/000146832726000031/rent-20260430.htm

findings.finding: FY26 guidance cuts rental product acquired to $45-50m from $74.9m in FY25 — a ~35% reduction in the inventory that is the product — while ending Active Subscriber growth has already decelerated from ~+20% y/y in Q4 FY25 to +5.8% y/y in Q1 FY26 (155,692), and the dominant live customer complaint is that the assortment is empty ('tiny inventory with items rarely available for rent', 'items marked available now that aren't available in any size').
findings.why_not_priced: The guidance line and the subscriber line are each in the wire; the linkage is not, and the linkage is what sets the Q3 subscriber guide given on 2026-09-11. The Q2 comp is 146,373 actives, which last year fell sequentially from Q1, so a flat sequential quarter still prints ~+6% y/y and the headline metric looks fine — the damage shows up in the forward guide, which is the part no one has modelled. If the market had connected the capex cut to churn there would be a subscriber estimate below the +5.8% trend in circulation; the only public framing is 'revenue up 29%'.
findings.independence: Different-source corroboration of the assortment problem, from customer-facing data rather than filings: https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/www.renttherunway.com . Note the revenue/subscriber divergence itself is visible in the same 2026-06-03 release as the guidance, so this finding rests on one press release plus one consumer source, not two filings.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider activity: all three 2026 Form 4s (2026-06-03, 2026-07-27, 2026-08-13) are RSU grants for board service, e.g. Rosensweig 35,481 RSUs at $0 on 2026-08-11 — no open-market buying and no open-market selling, so no Form 4 cluster either way
Going concern / substantial doubt: the Q1 FY26 10-Q contains no going-concern or substantial-doubt language and says management expects sufficient liquidity for at least twelve months

Covenant trip risk: dead end, and deliberately so — the minimum liquidity covenant was permanently removed by the 2026-01-28 First Amendment, so the $15m/$30m thresholds described in the Oct 2025 A&R are no longer in force and there is nothing to breach

Reverse split or authorized-share increase: the 2026-07-14 annual meeting approved elimination of unused Class B and preferred classes and an equity-plan reserve increase, not a reverse split or a capital increase
Identifiable news cause for the -28.5% five-session fall other than the 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-04 8-Ks — no Nasdaq notice, no index event and no article found
Option-implied expectation: baseline confirms no options market on RENT, so there is no skew to trade against
App-store download/ranking trend: no timely, dated, citable download or ranking series obtainable; only undated aggregate review scores, which I did not use as a standalone finding
baseline_tension: Everything I found agrees with the run-up rather than cutting against it — the tape is already down 28.5% in five sessions and sitting exactly on its 52-week low, so the two 8-Ks are demonstrably leaking into the price and only the pre-recorded-call format change and the Q2 cash arithmetic are plausibly untouched, which is why the sum is roughly half the 18.2% median reaction rather than a full one; the honest counterweight, which I did not file as a finding because there is no evidence of an actual transaction, is that the 2026-07-14 charter amendments removed supermajority voting and the written-consent prohibition and let 40% holders call special meetings, lowering the procedural bar for the CHS-led lender group to squeeze out minorities — a take-private headline is the upside tail and is why every impact_high is at or above zero.
